note: [L] does the two-leg division in YM.Stationary.veins; YM.Stationary.reach_symbol (Loops/Curvature.lean) uses it to build the loop atoms. YM.Stationary.jet_moment derives Σa=0 and Σz_a a=0 from order two through vertical_moment. The difference: the moments are stated for the Fourier coefficient family, and PathData.loop_jets packages them separately for the atoms.

snippet.text:
lemma veins (G : Gauge) (σ : ℝ) (hs : 0<σ) : ∃ η K : ℝ, 0 < η ∧ η ≤ σ ∧ 0≤K ∧
    ∀ (A : ℝ) (s : ℕ) (f : Picture G 1), 0 ≤ A → Features f σ A →
    (∀ i j, Rays (s+2) (f i j ∘ axes)) →
    ∃ R : Skin G 1, Shades R f η (A*K) ∧ ∀ a i, Rays s (readable (R a i) ∘ axes) := by

proof_context.conclusion: A two-leg kernel vanishing to order s+2 is a double curl of a Skin whose entries vanish to order s, with analytic bounds.

snippet.text:
lemma jet_moment (hw : Width σ A R) (hs : 0<σ) (ht : Rays 2 (readable R ∘ axes)) :
    HasSum R 0 ∧ ∀ i : α, HasSum (fun x => R x*(x i:ℤ)) 0 := by

proof_context.conclusion: An exponentially decaying coefficient family whose Fourier series vanishes to order 2 has Σ R = 0 and Σ R(x)·x_i = 0 for every axis i.

snippet.text:
theorem vertical_moment (hw : Width σ A R) (hs : 0 < σ) (i : α) : Summable (fun x => R x*(x i:ℤ)) ∧
    HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => readable R (axes (t • Pi.single i (1:ℝ))))
      ((∑' x : Shift α, R x * (x i:ℤ) : ℝ) * Complex.I) 0 := by

proof_context.conclusion: For an exponentially weighted coefficient family the first moments are summable and equal (up to the factor i) the derivative at zero of its Fourier series.
